result_semantic_payload.summary: Three of the four CRM orders are confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log via a verbatim order_id match, corroborated by an exact amount match in every case: ORD-70231 (wangqiang, 20000 USDT) ↔ 2024-06-01 settlement wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000; ORD-70232 (zhaolei, 15000) ↔ 2024-06-01 settlement wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000; ORD-70233 (sunli, 31500) ↔ 2024-06-02 settlement wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500. All three CRM rows are status=paid, consistent with a successful settlement. Two records must stay separate: (1) settlement line 2024-06-02 order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 — this order id does not exist in /crm/orders.csv, so per the task's own rule it cannot be treated as the same order and must not be merged into the CRM table; it is likely a typo of ORD-70233 (a transposition) but the evidence does not support that identification; (2) CRM order ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, status=cancelled) has no settlement counterpart, so it must not be reported as settled. Note the amount discrepancy: ORD-72033's 9999 ≠ ORD-70233's 31500, which is an additional reason the two cannot be linked.

claim_candidates.text: CRM order ORD-70231 (buyer wangqiang, 20000 USDT, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line '2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70231 wallet=TXabc111 amount=20000 ok'.
CRM order ORD-70232 (buyer zhaolei, 15000 USDT, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line '2024-06-01 settle order=ORD-70232 wallet=TXdef222 amount=15000 ok'.
CRM order ORD-70233 (buyer sunli, 31500 USDT, status paid) is confirmed by the settlement log line '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-70233 wallet=TXghi333 amount=31500 ok'.

The linkage key between CRM and settlement records is the order_id field, referenced verbatim in both sources; the amount_usdt value acts as an independent corroborating field and matches exactly for all three confirmed pairs.

Settlement log entry '2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok' must stay separate from the CRM orders because ORD-72033 does not exist in /crm/orders.csv; the README explicitly states a settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order.
CRM order ORD-70234 (buyer qianer, 8000 USDT, status cancelled) has no settlement counterpart and therefore must not be reported as settled by the payment processor.

The unmatched settlement ORD-72033 (amount 9999) is not amount-equivalent to any CRM order, including the visually similar ORD-70233 (31500); the id difference is a single-character transposition, but the evidence does not support identifying the two as the same order.
limitations: No additional reconciliation source (bank statement, processor API export) is present in the evidence set to resolve whether ORD-72033 is a typo, a distinct order, or a fraudulent/replayed settlement.

claim_candidates.text: All three settlement log lines carry status 'ok' and all three matched CRM rows carry status 'paid', which is internally consistent; no contradiction between CRM status and settlement outcome was observed.

limitations: The delegated source scope is labelled 'windows', but the task's task context reports no Windows platform scenario and no Windows-derived artifacts (registry, event logs, prefetch, amcache) are present; the evidence consists of three plain files on a generic filesystem image, so no Windows execution/account/persistence analysis was possible.
File mtimes are identical (1790594136) and all timeline events are a single synthetic CREATED cluster, so no meaningful temporal ordering between CRM writes and settlement entries can be established.
The evidence set contains only the settlement log as the payment-processor source; no processor API export, bank statement, or dispute record is available to adjudicate the unmatched ORD-72033 entry.
Amount units are recorded as USDT in the CRM and unlabelled in the settlement log; equivalence was assumed by numeric value only.
No prior secondary analyses exist for this task, so no independent reviewer findings were available to cross-check.
warnings: ORD-72033 vs ORD-70233 differ by a single transposed digit; automated fuzzy matching could wrongly merge them. They must remain separate pending processor-side confirmation.
ORD-70234 is status=cancelled with no settlement; it must not be counted as settled revenue.
